issues.description: The mimeType request parameter is still reflected verbatim into the response Content-Type header (getMimeType unchanged); the official fix added MimeTypeUtil.sanitize restricting it to application/json or text/plain to close a secondary content-sniffing XSS vector. Our patch does not address this path.

On an invalid callback the patch silently degrades to a plain (non-JSONP) response instead of rejecting the request with an error as the official fix does; behavior-preserving and safe, but a client sending a bad callback gets an unwrapped body rather than an explicit failure.

Execution evidence is weak: pov_before_reproduced=false and regressions_ran=0 (regressions_passed=null), so vulnerability closure and regression safety rest on code reasoning and the added tests rather than pipeline confirmation.

result.summary: Our patch is a substantively correct fix for the primary CVE-2018-1000129 callback XSS: it validates the JSONP callback against an anchored JavaScript-identifier allowlist at every embedding sink (AgentServlet non-streaming, IoUtil streaming, and the jvm JolokiaHttpHandler), which is the defense-of-record for this JSONP context and matches the official regex intent. It differs by gracefully falling back to plain JSON instead of throwing, and — more importantly — it does not replicate the official MimeTypeUtil mimeType sanitization, leaving a secondary Content-Type-based XSS vector unaddressed. Net: sound and minimal for the callback vector, but a weaker subset of the official fix.
result.root_cause: Untrusted `callback` request parameter is concatenated unescaped into the JavaScript/JSONP response body (and the mimeType parameter into Content-Type), so a correct fix must constrain the callback to a safe JS-identifier at the sink and sanitize the response content type.
